## FAQ

### What are the best alternatives to Entrepreneur First?

Foundinity if what you want is a cofounder. For a programme: Antler (full-time team forming), South Park Commons, ODF and Z Fellows (communities and short programmes for people before an idea), Conception X and Startup Wise Guys' Founders Club (part-time), Startup Weekend (a weekend), and venture studios such as Hexa.

### Who are Entrepreneur First's competitors?

Antler is the closest: it also takes individuals and helps them form teams in a full-time residency. South Park Commons competes for the same people at the stage before an idea. Accelerators such as Y Combinator and Techstars are often named, but they take teams, not individuals.

### Is Antler better than Entrepreneur First? [...] | \# | Option | How you meet a cofounder | Cost to join, or what it takes | Format and length | Where |
---------|
| 1 | Foundinity | Ranked by compatibility on multiple dimensions around who you are and how you work | Free to get started; Plus $5 a week or $15 a month | No cohort, no end date | Online |

| 3 | South Park Commons Residency | A community of people exploring before an idea | No fees or dues | 6 months, expected in person through the week | San Francisco, New York, Bangalore | [...] 1\. If you mainly want a cofounder and can't quit or move, start with Foundinity. 2. If you can go full-time and want EF's format somewhere else, look at Antler, and check your country's page: the UK FAQ says it backs solo founders "with a solid idea or a product already in market", though another line on the same page says arriving with the idea still taking shape is fine. 3. If you want to explore before an idea, in a community, South Park Commons suits people who can be in San Francisco, New York or Bangalore for six months; ODF and Z Fellows compress it into a week. 4. If you're a researcher with a technology, Conception X runs alongside a PhD and costs nothing. 5. If you want structure while you keep your job, the Founders Club is paid and weekly; Startup Weekend is one weekend. 6.

### 2. Founder Institute's online cofounder events

What it is. Virtual networking events for people looking for a cofounder, open to anyone.

What to know. Founder Institute states that it doesn't guarantee you'll find a cofounder. The events are for meeting people; any follow-up is up to you.

Where Foundinity differs. An hour of networking tells you little about how someone works. On Foundinity, the compatibility breakdown shows that before you spend time on a call. [...] Where Foundinity differs. Everyone on Foundinity is there for a cofounder, now or later, and your profile isn't public, so you can look while you're still employed. See LinkedIn vs Foundinity.

### 6. Entrepreneur First and Antler

What they are. Full-time programmes that take individuals and help them form teams. Antler's UK residency runs for up to eight weeks, in person.

What to know. Both are selective; Antler says it backs under 1% of applicants. Both expect you full-time, which usually means leaving your job first. Entrepreneur First also asks you to move to one of its hub cities.
